work.permit: Licence from the Ministry of Labour

note: Work: Decent Work Act, 2015 (which repealed Title 18 of the Executive Law, the Labour Practices Law), read in the copy liblaw.org publishes (the Ministry of Labour's and the Legislature's sites didn't answer today): § 21.2, no person shall employ or allow a child under 15 to be employed in full-time employment; § 21.3, a child of at least 13 may do light work on conditions. The Children's Law, 2011 (read in the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection's copy), section 9.3: any contract of apprenticeship or employment of a child (a person under 18) needs a parent's or guardian's consent and a licence from the Ministry of Labour. Neither law names performers; a performer under 15 is held as allowed on the Ministry's licence (a reading: § 21.2 bars only full-time employment under 15, and the Children's Law puts every child's employment under licence), with no lower age set. Hours limits aren't held. Majority: not read; the Children's Law defines a child as under 18 for its own purposes, and no statute setting the age of majority was found. Service: not read; no Liberian law calling anyone to military service was found.

sources.title: Decent Work Act, 2015 (copy published by liblaw.org)
sources.said: § 21.2 Minimum Age for Employment No person shall employ, or allow a child under the age of 15 years to be employed in full time employment. § 21.3 Light work for children under the age of 15 a) A child who is at least 13 years old may be employed to perform light work

sources.title: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Children's Law of Liberia, 2011
sources.said: “Child” shall mean any person below the age of 18 years ... 9.3 Any contract for apprenticeship or employment shall be with the consent of the child’s parent or guardian, consistent with the provisions of subsections 1 and 2 of this section and all other applicable laws and regulations, and under license from the Ministry of Labor.
